title: Do You Panic When You Share Your Location?
description: Discover your privacy calculus type based on how you manage your digital footprint.

questions.text: You snap a great cafe pic, but a street sign is in the background. What do you do?

choices.label: Post immediately! Let people know where it is.
Post it later when I get home.
Crop it, blur the sign, panic, then post.
Delete it entirely. Too risky.

questions.text: A friend tags your exact location on a public story. Reaction?

choices.label: Repost it immediately!
Ask them to untag me if I'm still there.
Instantly remove the tag and sweat nervously.
My friends know better than to tag me.

questions.text: Your real-time location sharing map is...

choices.label: On for everyone, always.
On, but strictly for close friends.
Turns on by accident, turns off in fear.
Disabled at the system level.

questions.text: You take a mirror selfie in your bedroom. What's the protocol?

choices.label: Room tour time! Show it all.
Ensure no mail or address labels are visible.
Zoom in and double-check everything 5 times.
Blank white wall only. No context.

questions.text: The main reason you manage your digital footprint is...

choices.label: I don't. Let them watch.
Safety first, aesthetics second.
Fear of stalkers and weirdos finding me.
I enjoy being an unsolvable mystery.
